sanskrit: sadyo ha jāto vṛṣabhaḥ kanīnaḥ prabhartum āvad andhasaḥ sutasya | sādhoḥ piba pratikāmaṁ yathā te rasāśiraḥ prathamaṁ somyasya ||
english: Scarce born, the bull, the youthful one, was eager to bear away the pressed Soma juice; drink, as pleases thee, O potent one, the first draught of the excellent Soma blended with milk.

sanskrit: yaj jāyathās tad ahar asya kāme 'ṁśoḥ pīyūṣam apibo giriṣṭhām | taṁ te mātā pari yoṣā janitrī mahaḥ pitur dama āsiñcad agre ||
english: On that very day when thou wast born, in thy desire thou drankest the first milk of the Soma stalk that grows on the mountain; that milk, O youth, thy mother, thy genetrix, poured out for thee first in the great father's house.

sanskrit: upasthāya mātaram annam aiṭṭa tigmam apaśyad abhi somam ūdhaḥ | prayāvayann acarad gṛtso anyān mahāni cakre purudhapratīkaḥ ||
english: Coming to his mother he sought food; sharp-eyed, he beheld the udder of the Soma; driving others away he moved on, the impetuous one, manifold in aspect — he accomplished great deeds.

sanskrit: ugras turāṣāḻ abhibhūtyojā yathāvaśaṁ tanvaṁ cakra eṣaḥ | tvaṣṭāram indro januṣābhibhūyāmuṣyā somam apibac camūṣu ||
english: Fierce, the crusher of strongholds, overpowering in might, he shaped his body as he willed; Indra, having overcome Tvaṣṭṛ at his very birth, drank the Soma from his bowls.

sanskrit: śunaṁ huvema maghavānam indram asmin bhare nṛtamaṁ vājasātau | śṛṇvantam ugram ūtaye samatsu ghnantaṁ vṛtrāṇi saṁjitaṁ dhanānām ||
english: With blessing let us call Indra the bountiful, the foremost hero in this contest for the prize; him who hearkens, the fierce one, for our aid in battles — slayer of Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.

sanskrit: śaṁsā mahām indraṁ yasmin viśvā ā kṛṣṭayaḥ somapāḥ kāmam avyan | yaṁ sukratuṁ dhiṣaṇe vibhvataṣṭaṁ ghanaṁ vṛtrāṇāṁ janayanta devāḥ ||
english: Proclaim the greatness of Indra in whom all Soma-drinking peoples find their full desire; him of keen purpose, wrought wide by Dhiṣaṇā, the destroyer of Vṛtras, whom the gods brought to birth.

sanskrit: yaṁ nu nakiḥ pṛtanāsu svarājaṁ dvitā tarati nṛtamaṁ hariṣṭhām | inatamaḥ satvabhir yo ha śūṣaiḥ pṛthujrayā aminād āyur dasyoḥ ||
english: Whom none at all in battles overcomes — the self-ruler, foremost of heroes, standing in the tawny steeds; who, most powerful with his fighters and shouts, with far-extending flame cut short the life of the Dasyu.

sanskrit: sahāvā pṛtsu taraṇir nārvā vyānaśī rodasī mehanāvān | bhago na kāre havyo matīnām piteva cāruḥ suhavo vayodhāḥ ||
english: Prevailing in battles, the rapid one, not to be overcome, he who fills both worlds with his greatness; to be invoked as Bhaga in the rite, worthy of the prayers, dear as a father, easy of invocation, the bestower of strength.

sanskrit: dhartā divo rajasas pṛṣṭa ūrdhvo ratho na vāyur vasubhir niyutvān | kṣapāṁ vastā janitā sūryasya vibhaktā bhāgaṁ dhiṣaṇeva vājam ||
english: The upholder of heaven, exalted upon the back of the firmament, like a chariot of wind yoked with good steeds; he who clothes the night, the begetter of the Sun, the distributor of shares like Dhiṣaṇā distributes the prize.

sanskrit: śunaṁ huvema maghavānam indram asmin bhare nṛtamaṁ vājasātau | śṛṇvantam ugram ūtaye samatsu ghnantaṁ vṛtrāṇi saṁjitaṁ dhanānām ||
english: With blessing let us call Indra the bountiful, the foremost hero in this contest for the prize; him who hearkens, the fierce one, for our aid in battles — slayer of Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.

sanskrit: indraḥ svāhā pibatu yasya soma āgatyā tumro vṛṣabho marutvān | oruvyacāḥ pṛṇatām ebhir annair āsya havis tanva1ḥ kāmam ṛdhyāḥ ||
english: Let Indra, svāhā, drink of him whose Soma is pressed — the strong bull accompanied by the Maruts, who has come hither; wide-reaching, may he satisfy us with these foods; may the oblation of thy body prosper according to desire.

sanskrit: ā te saparyū javase yunajmi yayor anu pradivaḥ śruṣṭim āvaḥ | iha tvā dheyur harayaḥ suśipra pibā tv a1sya suṣutasya cāroḥ ||
english: I yoke for thee thy two worshipful steeds for speed, through whom thou hast ever followed obedience from of old; may the bay steeds bring thee here, O fair-lipped one; drink now of this, the beautifully pressed Soma.

sanskrit: gobhir mimikṣuṁ dadhire supāram indraṁ jyaiṣṭhyāya dhāyase gṛṇānāḥ | mandānaḥ somam papivām ṛjīṣin sam asmabhyam purudhā gā iṣaṇya ||
english: The singers, mixing him with milk, established Indra, easy to cross over, for supreme nourishment; thou who art gladdened, who hast drunk the Soma, O Ṛjīṣin, drive together for us the cows in manifold ways.

sanskrit: imaṁ kāmam mandayā gobhir aśvaiś candravatā rādhasā paprathaś ca | svaryavo matibhis tubhyaṁ viprā indrāya vāhaḥ kuśikāso akran ||
english: Gladden this desire with cows and horses and with thy brilliant gift that is extended far; the inspired Kuśikas have made their conveyances for Indra with joyous hymns of praise to thee.

sanskrit: śunaṁ huvema maghavānam indram asmin bhare nṛtamaṁ vājasātau | śṛṇvantam ugram ūtaye samatsu ghnantaṁ vṛtrāṇi saṁjitaṁ dhanānām ||
english: With blessing let us call Indra the bountiful, the foremost hero in this contest for the prize; him who hearkens, the fierce one, for our aid in battles — slayer of Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.

sanskrit: carṣaṇīdhṛtam maghavānam ukthya1m indraṁ giro bṛhatīr abhy anūṣata | vāvṛdhānam puruhūtaṁ suvṛktibhir amartyaṁ jaramāṇaṁ dive-dive ||
english: The broad hymns have sung forth in praise of Indra, the bountiful, cherished by all peoples, worthy of laud; him who ever waxes strong, invoked by many, with beautiful praises — the immortal one who is lauded day by day.

sanskrit: śatakratum arṇavaṁ śākinaṁ naraṁ giro ma indram upa yanti viśvataḥ | vājasanim pūrbhidaṁ tūrṇim apturaṁ dhāmasācam abhiṣācaṁ svarvidam ||
english: My hymns approach Indra from all sides — the man of a hundred powers, the flood-like, the mighty, the winner of prizes, the breaker of strongholds, the swift, the one never missed, abiding in the dwelling, united with glory, the finder of light.

sanskrit: ākare vasor jaritā panasyate 'nehasaḥ stubha indro duvasyati | vivasvataḥ sadana ā hi pipriye satrāsāham abhimātihanaṁ stuhi ||
english: At the mine of riches the singer is celebrated; Indra, blameless, is pleased with praises and gives service; for he delights in the dwelling of Vivasvat — praise him who conquers all, who slays the assailants.

sanskrit: nṛṇām u tvā nṛtamaṁ gīrbhir ukthair abhi pra vīram arcatā sabādhaḥ | saṁ sahase purumāyo jihīte namo asya pradiva eka īśe ||
english: Sing forth together with hymns and lauds the hero, the foremost of men; he who is full of craft springs up to meet your strength; reverence to him who alone is lord from of old.

sanskrit: pūrvīr asya niṣṣidho martyeṣu purū vasūni pṛthivī bibharti | indrāya dyāva oṣadhīr utāpo rayiṁ rakṣanti jīrayo vanāni ||
english: Many are his resting-places among mortals; the earth bears many treasures for him; the skies, the herbs, the waters, the swift streams, and the forests guard the wealth for Indra.

sanskrit: tubhyam brahmāṇi gira indra tubhyaṁ satrā dadhire harivo juṣasva | bodhy ā3pir avaso nūtanasya sakhe vaso jaritṛbhyo vayo dhāḥ ||
english: For thee are these prayers and hymns, O Indra; for thee entirely have they been established, O lord of bays — be pleased with them; be an ally for the help of the new song, O friend, O Vasu; bestow vigour upon the singers.

sanskrit: indra marutva iha pāhi somaṁ yathā śāryāte apibaḥ sutasya | tava praṇītī tava śūra śarmann ā vivāsanti kavayaḥ suyajñāḥ ||
english: Indra, with thy Marut host, drink here the Soma as thou drankest of what was pressed for Śāryāta; under thy leadership, in thy protection, O hero, the wise poets who sacrifice well seek favour.

sanskrit: sa vāvaśāna iha pāhi somam marudbhir indra sakhibhiḥ sutaṁ naḥ | jātaṁ yat tvā pari devā abhūṣan mahe bharāya puruhūta viśve ||
english: He, eagerly desiring, drink here the Soma pressed for us, O Indra, with thy friends the Maruts; when the gods adorned thee at birth for the great contest, O much-invoked, all of them.

sanskrit: aptūrye maruta āpir eṣo 'mandann indram anu dātivārāḥ | tebhiḥ sākam pibatu vṛtrakhādaḥ sutaṁ somaṁ dāśuṣaḥ sve sadhasthe ||
english: In the rite of the waters these Maruts are his allies, the givers of gifts, who gladden Indra; may the devourer of Vṛtra drink together with them the pressed Soma of the worshipper in his own dwelling place.

sanskrit: idaṁ hy anv ojasā sutaṁ rādhānām pate | pibā tv a1sya girvaṇaḥ ||
english: This indeed has been pressed with strength, O lord of bounties; drink now of this, O thou who art praised with hymns.

sanskrit: yas te anu svadhām asat sute ni yaccha tanvam | sa tvā mamattu somyam ||
english: Whosoever shall be with thee according to thy will at the pressing, pour thyself down upon him; let him delight in thee who art full of Soma.

sanskrit: pra te aśnotu kukṣyoḥ prendra brahmaṇā śiraḥ | pra bāhū śūra rādhase ||
english: Let the sacred prayer penetrate thy two flanks, O Indra, and thy head; and reach thy two arms, O hero, for the bestowal of bounty.

sanskrit: dhānāvantaṁ karambhiṇam apūpavantam ukthinam | indra prātar juṣasva naḥ ||
english: The offering with parched grain, the mixture with groats, the cake, together with the laud — be pleased with these of ours at dawn, O Indra.

sanskrit: puroḻāśam pacatyaṁ juṣasvendrā gurasva ca | tubhyaṁ havyāni sisrate ||
english: The cake to be cooked, O Indra — be pleased with it and accept it; for thee the oblations are poured out.

sanskrit: puroḻāśaṁ ca no ghaso joṣayāse giraś ca naḥ | vadhūyur iva yoṣaṇām ||
english: Enjoy our sacrificial cake and delight in our hymns, as a bridegroom delights in maidens.

sanskrit: puroḻāśaṁ sanaśruta prātaḥsāve juṣasva naḥ | indra kratur hi te bṛhan ||
english: The sacrificial cake at the morning pressing — be pleased with ours, O thou who hast been praised of old; for thy will, O Indra, is great.

sanskrit: mādhyaṁdinasya savanasya dhānāḥ puroḻāśam indra kṛṣveha cārum | pra yat stotā jaritā tūrṇyartho vṛṣāyamāṇa upa gīrbhir īṭṭe ||
english: Make the parched grains and the sacrificial cake of the midday pressing beautiful here, O Indra; when the praiser, the singer, swift of purpose, desiring thee, approaches thee with hymns.

sanskrit: tṛtīye dhānāḥ savane puruṣṭuta puroḻāśam āhutam māmahasva naḥ | ṛbhumantaṁ vājavantaṁ tvā kave prayasvanta upa śikṣema dhītibhiḥ ||
english: At the third pressing the parched grains and the offered cake — exalt us, O thou who art praised by many; thee, O sage, who art accompanied by the Ṛbhus and prizes, may we approach with our prayers, bearing oblations.

sanskrit: pūṣaṇvate te cakṛmā karambhaṁ harivate haryaśvāya dhānāḥ | apūpam addhi sagaṇo marudbhiḥ somam piba vṛtrahā śūra vidvān ||
english: We have made the groat-mixture for thee who art accompanied by Pūṣan, and the parched grain for thee who lovest the bay steeds; eat the cake with thy company of Maruts; drink the Soma, O hero, slayer of Vṛtra, thou who knowest.

sanskrit: prati dhānā bharata tūyam asmai puroḻāśaṁ vīratamasya nṛṇām | dive-dive sadṛśīr indra tubhyaṁ vardhantu tvā somapeyāya dhṛṣṇo ||
english: Bring quickly to him the parched grains and the cake — to him who is the most heroic of men; day by day may the fitting offerings increase thee, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma, O bold one.

sanskrit: indrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena vāmīr iṣa ā vahataṁ suvīrāḥ | vītaṁ havyāni adhvareṣu devā vardhe thāṁ gīrbhir iḻayā madantā ||
english: O Indra and Parvata, bring here with the great chariot the choicest refreshments, ye who bestow good heroes; enjoy the oblations at the rites, O gods; may ye two wax great, gladdened by our hymns and by Iḷā.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhā su kam maghavan mā parā gāḥ somasya nu tvā suṣutasya yakṣi | pitur na putraḥ sicam ā rabhe ta indra svādiṣṭhayā girā śacīvaḥ ||
english: Stay well, O bountiful one, do not pass away; I will now sacrifice to thee with the beautifully pressed Soma; as a son grasps his father's skirt, so I take hold of thee, O Indra, O powerful one, with the sweetest hymn.

sanskrit: śaṁsāvādhvaryo prati me gṛṇīhīndrāya vāhaḥ kṛṇavāva juṣṭam | edam barhir yajamānasya sīdāthā ca bhūd uktham indrāya śastam ||
english: Let us two recite, O Adhvaryu, answer my words; let us make the chariot-offering agreeable to Indra; let Indra sit on this sacrificial grass of the sacrificer, and then let the laud be proclaimed to Indra.

sanskrit: jāyed astam maghavan sed u yonis tad it tvā yuktā harayo vahantu | yadā kadā ca sunavāma somam agniṣ ṭvā dūto dhanvāty accha ||
english: The wife is the home, O bountiful one, and she is the womb — may the yoked bay steeds bring thee there; whenever we press the Soma, may Agni as messenger speed toward thee.

sanskrit: parā yāhi maghavann ā ca yāhīndra bhrātar ubhayatrā te artham | yatrā rathasya bṛhato nidhānaṁ vimocanaṁ vājino rāsabhasya ||
english: Depart and return, O bountiful one; O Indra, O brother, thy purpose lies in both directions — both where the great chariot is put to rest and where the prize-winning horse is unyoked.

sanskrit: apāḥ somam astam indra pra yāhi kalyāṇīr jāyā suraṇaṁ gṛhe te | yatrā rathasya bṛhato nidhānaṁ vimocanaṁ vājino dakṣiṇāvat ||
english: Thou hast drunk the Soma; proceed home, O Indra; a fair wife awaits thee joyfully in thy house — where the great chariot is laid to rest and the prize horse is unyoked on the right side.

sanskrit: ime bhojā aṅgiraso virūpā divas putrāso asurasya vīrāḥ | viśvāmitrāya dadato maghāni sahasrasāve pra tiranta āyuḥ ||
english: These Bhoja princes of various forms, sons of heaven, heroes of the lord of might — giving gifts to Viśvāmitra, they extend their life to a thousandfold pressing.

sanskrit: rūpaṁ-rūpam maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānas tanvam pari svām | trir yad divaḥ pari muhūrtam āgāt svair mantrair anṛtupā ṛtāvā ||
english: The bountiful one assumes form after form, working his wonders about his own body; when he has come three times around heaven for a moment — he who seasons not the seasons, yet the master of holy law, by his own spells.

sanskrit: mahām̐ ṛṣir devajā devajūto 'stabhnāt sindhuṁ arṇavaṁ nṛcakṣāḥ | viśvāmitro yad avahad sudāsam apriyāyata kuśikebhir indraḥ ||
english: The great seer, god-born and god-driven, beholding men, stayed the flooded river Sindhu; when Viśvāmitra was conveying Sudās, Indra became friendly through the Kuśikas.

sanskrit: haṁsā iva kṛṇutha ślokam adribhir madanto gīrbhir adhvare sute sacā | devebhir viprā ṛṣayo nṛcakṣaso vi pibadhvaṁ kuśikāḥ somyam madhu ||
english: Like swans ye make your sound with the pressing stones, gladdened at the rite when the Soma has been pressed together with hymns; O inspired sages, seers who behold men, O Kuśikas, drink separately the sweet Soma mead.

sanskrit: upa preta kuśikāś cetayadhvam aśvaṁ rāye pra muñcatā sudāsaḥ | rājā vṛtraṁ jaṅghanat prāg apāg udag athā yajāte vara ā pṛthivyāḥ ||
english: Come near, O Kuśikas, be attentive; release the horse of Sudās for wealth; the king has slain the foe to east, to west, and to the north — now let him sacrifice in the choicest place of the earth.

sanskrit: ya ime rodasī ubhe aham indram atuṣṭavam | viśvāmitrasya rakṣati brahme dam bhāratam janam ||
english: I who have praised Indra — both these worlds — the sacred prayer of Viśvāmitra protects the people of Bharata.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrā arāsata brahmendrāya vajriṇe | karad in naḥ surādhasaḥ ||
english: The Viśvāmitras have offered the sacred prayer to Indra who wields the thunderbolt; may he make us rich in good bounty.

sanskrit: kiṁ te kṛṇvanti kīkaṭeṣu gāvo nāśiraṁ duhre na tapanti gharmam | ā no bhara pramagandasya vedo naicāśākham maghavan randhayā naḥ ||
english: What do the cows do for thee among the Kīkaṭas? They yield no admixture of milk, nor do they heat the ritual drink; bring us the wealth of Pramaganda, O bountiful one, and subdue for us the low-branched one.

sanskrit: sasarparīr amatim bādhamānā bṛhan mimāya jamadagnidattā | ā sūryasya duhitā tatāna śravo deveṣv amṛtam ajuryam ||
english: The far-spreading one, given by Jamadagni, having repelled ignorance, measured out greatly; the daughter of the Sun stretched out fame that is immortal and undecaying among the gods.

sanskrit: sasarparīr abharat tūyam ebhyo 'dhi śravaḥ pāñcajanyāsu kṛṣṭiṣu | sā pakṣyā3 navyam āyur dadhānā yām me palastijamadagnayo daduḥ ||
english: The far-spreading one quickly brought fame to these five peoples; bearing new life for the wing, which the Palastis and Jamadagnīs gave to me.

sanskrit: sthirau gāvau bhavatāṁ vīḻur akṣo meṣā vi varhi mā yugaṁ vi śāri | indraḥ pātalye dadatāṁ śarītor ariṣṭaneme abhi naḥ sacasva ||
english: May the two oxen be firm, the axle strong; remove the ram, let not the yoke be shattered; may Indra give what is hidden in the peg-hole — O thou whose wheel-rim is uninjured, be thou with us.

sanskrit: balaṁ dhehi tanūṣu no balam indrānaḻutsu naḥ | balaṁ tokāya tanayāya jīvase tvaṁ hi baladā asi ||
english: Place strength in our bodies, O Indra, place strength in our bulls; place strength in our immediate offspring and in our descendants for life — for thou art the giver of strength.

sanskrit: abhi vyayasva khadirasya sāram ojo dhehi spandane śiṁśapāyām | akṣa vīḻo vīḻita vīḻayasva mā yāmād asmād ava jīhipo naḥ ||
english: Wrap thyself in the heartwood of the Khadira tree; place thy strength in the trembling Śiṁśapā wood; axle, O firm one, be firmly made firm; do not slip away from this chariot of ours.

sanskrit: ayam asmān vanaspatiḥ mā ca hā mā ca rīriṣat | svasty ā gṛhebhya āvasā ā vimocānāt ||
english: Let this forest tree neither abandon us nor injure us; may it bring us safely, with good shelter, from house to the place of unyoking.

sanskrit: indrotibhir bahulābhir no adya yācchreṣṭhābhir maghavañ chūra jinva | yo no dveṣṭy adhara sas padīṣṭa yam u dviṣmas tam u prāṇo jahātu ||
english: Quicken us today, O Indra, with thy many aids, with the best of them, O bountiful one, O hero; let him who hates us fall low; and him whom we hate — let his own breath forsake him.

sanskrit: paraśuṁ cid vi tapati śimbalaṁ cid vi vṛścati | ukhā cid indra yeṣantī prayastā phenam asyati ||
english: Even the axe splits apart; even the silk-cotton tree is cut through; even the cooking-pot, O Indra, when it rushes forward, well offered, throws off its foam.

sanskrit: na sāyakasya cikite janāso lodhaṁ nayanti paśu manyamānāḥ | nāvājinaṁ vājinā hāsayanti na gardabham puro aśvān nayanti ||
english: People understand not the arrow; thinking it an animal, they lead the Lodha tree; they do not put the non-prize-winner to shame with the prize-winner, nor do they place the donkey before the horses.

sanskrit: ima indra bharatasya putrā apapitvaṁ cikitur na papritvam | hinvanty aśvam araṇaṁ na nityaṁ jyāvājam pari ṇayanty ājau ||
english: These sons of Bharata, O Indra, have understood retreat, not advance; they urge the horse like a wild, not domestic one, and lead around the bowstring-impelled one in battle.

sanskrit: imam mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṁ śaśvat kṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruḥ | śṛṇotu no damyebhir anīkaiḥ śṛṇotv agnir divyair ajasraḥ ||
english: They have sung forth this strength for the great, ever-adorable one, again and again; may he hear us with his domestic hosts; may Agni, the inextinguishable one, hear us with his heavenly hosts.

sanskrit: mahi mahe dive arcā pṛthivyai kāmo ma icchaññ carati prajānan | yayor ha stome vidatheṣu devāḥ saparyavo mādayante sacāyoḥ ||
english: Greatly do I sing in praise of great Heaven and Earth; my desire wanders knowing what it seeks; in their laud, at the assemblies, the gods who worship delight together in both of them.

sanskrit: yuvor ṛtaṁ rodasī satyam astu mahe ṣu ṇaḥ suvitāya pra bhūtam | idaṁ dive namo agne pṛthivyai saparyāmi prayasā yāmi ratnam ||
english: Let the holy law of you two, O Heaven and Earth, be true; be ye great for our great well-being; I pay homage to Heaven and to Earth, O Agni; I seek with offerings, I approach for the treasure.

sanskrit: uto hi vām pūrvyā āvividra ṛtāvarī rodasī satyavācaḥ | naraś cid vāṁ samithe śūrasātau vavandire pṛthivi vevidānāḥ ||
english: For your ancient ones have found you, O Heaven and Earth who keep holy law and speak truth; even heroes have praised you both in the assembly at the contest of heroes, O Earth, knowing you well.

sanskrit: ko addhā veda ka iha pravocad devām̐ acchā pathyā3 kā sam eti | dadṛśra eṣām avamā sadāṁsi pare ṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu ||
english: Who truly knows, who here could declare which path leads toward the gods? Their lowest seats are seen, those that are in the higher, secret observances.

sanskrit: kavir nṛcakṣā abhi ṣīm acaṣṭa ṛtasya yonā vighṛte madantī | nānā cakrāte sadanaṁ yathā veḥ samānena kratunā saṁvidāne ||
english: The seer who beholds men has looked upon them both, delighting in the ample source of holy law; like a bird's two wings, they have made their dwelling separate, yet with one purpose, understanding each other.

sanskrit: samānyā viyute dūreante dhruve pade tasthutur jāgarūke | uta svasārā yuvatī bhavantī ād u bruvāte mithunāni nāma ||
english: Of the same origin yet parted, far and near, they stand in the firm, wakeful station; and the two sisters, being young maidens, utter the names of the couples.

sanskrit: viśved ete janimā saṁ vivikto maho devān bibhratī na vyathete | ejad dhruvaṁ patyate viśvam ekaṁ carat patratri viṣuṇaṁ vi jātam ||
english: All this origin has become clearly distinguished; bearing the great gods, they do not totter; one thing, moving yet firm, rules the universe; another moving, winged, is born in various directions.

sanskrit: sanā purāṇam adhy emy ārān mahaḥ pitur janitur jāmi tan naḥ | devāso yatra panitāra evair urau pathi vyute tasthur antaḥ ||
english: I approach from afar the ancient thing of old, the kinship with the great father and begetter; where the gods, marvelling with their wonders, have stood apart in the wide path, between the two.

sanskrit: imaṁ stomaṁ rodasī pra bravīmy ṛdūdarāḥ śṛṇavann agnijijhvāḥ | mitraḥ samrājo varuṇo yuvānā ādityāsaḥ kavayaḥ paprathānāḥ ||
english: I speak this hymn to Heaven and Earth, may they with gentle bellies, with Agni as their tongue, hear it — Mitra, the young sovereign Varuṇa, the Ādityas who are wise seers, spread widely.

sanskrit: hiraṇyapāṇiḥ savitā sujihvas trir ā divo vidathe patya mānaḥ | deveṣu ca savitaḥ ślokam aśrer ād asmabhyam ā suva sarvatātim ||
english: Savitṛ of golden hands, of good tongue, ruling in the assembly three times from heaven; and O Savitṛ, thou who hast spread thy fame among the gods — now drive toward us all-embracing totality.

sanskrit: sukṛt supāṇiḥ svavām̐ ṛtāvā devas tvaṣṭāvase tāni no dhāt | pūṣaṇvanta ṛbhavo mādayadhvam ūrdhvagrāvāṇo adhvaram ataṣṭa ||
english: The god Tvaṣṭṛ, the well-doer, of fair hands, possessed of goodness, guardian of holy law — may he set these things for our help; O Ṛbhus accompanied by Pūṣan, be ye gladdened; with upraised pressing stones ye have fashioned the sacrifice.

sanskrit: vidyudra thā maruta ṛṣṭimanto divo maryā ṛtajātā ayāsaḥ | sarasvatī śṛṇavan yajñiyāso dhātā rayiṁ sahavīraṁ turāsaḥ ||
english: The Maruts, whose chariots are lightning, armed with spears, the youths of heaven, born of holy law, untiring; may Sarasvatī hear them, the worthy of worship; may Dhātṛ, the victorious, grant wealth accompanied by heroes.

sanskrit: viṣṇuṁ stomāsaḥ purudasmam arkā bhagasyeva kāriṇo yāmani gman | urukramaḥ kakuho yasya pūrvīr na mardhanti yuvatayo janitrīḥ ||
english: Hymns and praises have come to Viṣṇu of many wonders on his path, like those of Bhaga's worshippers; the wide-striding one who is the summit — his many young mothers who bore him never fail him.

sanskrit: indro viśvair vīryai3ḥ patyamāna ubhe ā paprau rodasī mahitvā | puraṁdaro vṛtrahā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇaḥ saṁgṛbhyā na ā bharā bhūri paśvaḥ ||
english: Indra, ruling with all his heroic powers, has filled both worlds with his greatness; the breaker of strongholds, the slayer of Vṛtra, of bold army — grasping firmly, bring us many cattle.

sanskrit: nāsatyā me pitarā bandhupṛcchā sajātyam aśvinoś cāru nāma | yuvaṁ hi stho rayidau no rayīṇāṁ dātraṁ rakṣethe akavair adabdhā ||
english: The two Nāsatyas are my fathers, to be asked of kin; the lovely name of the Aśvins is of the same clan; for ye two are the givers of riches to us among the wealthy; ye guard the gift, unblind and undeceived.

sanskrit: mahat tad vaḥ kavayaś cāru nāma yad dha devā bhavatha viśva indre | sakha ṛbhubhiḥ puruhūta priyebhir imāṁ dhiyaṁ sātaye takṣatā naḥ ||
english: That lovely name of yours is great, O wise ones, whereby ye all, O gods, are present in Indra; O friend, O much-invoked, with thy beloved Ṛbhus, fashion this thought of ours for victory.

sanskrit: aryamā ṇo aditir yajñiyāso 'dabdhāni varuṇasya vratāni | yuyota no anapatyāni gantoḥ prajāvān naḥ paśumām̐ astu gātuḥ ||
english: Aryaman, Aditi, the worthy of worship, the undeceived ordinances of Varuṇa — ward off from us childlessness and going away; may our path be fruitful in offspring and rich in cattle.

sanskrit: devānāṁ dūtaḥ purudhā prasūto 'nāgān no vocatu sarvatātā | śṛṇotu naḥ pṛthivī dyaur utāpaḥ sūryo nakṣatrair urv antari kṣam ||
english: May the messenger of the gods, sent forth in many ways, declare our freedom from guilt in all wholeness; may Earth hear us, and Heaven, and the Waters, the Sun, and the wide atmosphere with the stars.

sanskrit: śṛṇvantu no vṛṣaṇaḥ parvatāso dhruvakṣemāsa iḻayā madantaḥ | ādityair no aditiḥ śṛṇotu yacchantu no marutaḥ śarma bhadram ||
english: May the bull-like mountains hear us, those of firm abode, gladdened by Iḷā; may Aditi hear us together with the Ādityas; may the Maruts grant us excellent shelter.

sanskrit: sadā sugaḥ pitumām̐ astu panthā madhvā devā oṣadhīḥ sam pipṛkta | bhago me agne sakhye na mṛdhyā ud rāyo aśyāṁ sadanam purukṣoḥ ||
english: May the path ever be easily traversable and full of nourishment; may the gods mingle the herbs with sweetness; O Bhaga, O Agni, fail me not in thy friendship; may I attain the abode of riches, the seat of plenty.

sanskrit: svadāsva havyā sam iṣo didīhy asmadrya1k sam mimīhi śravāṁsi | viśvām̐ agne pṛtsu tāñ jeṣi śatrūn ahā viśvā sumanā dīdihī naḥ ||
english: Savour the oblations, kindle the refreshments, measure out the glories toward us; O Agni, conquer all those enemies in battles; shine upon us graciously through all the days.

sanskrit: uṣasaḥ pūrvā adha yad vyūṣur mahad vi jajñe akṣaram pade goḥ | vratā devānām upa nu prabhūṣan mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: From the former dawns — when they dawned — the great imperishable was born at the station of the cow; the ordinances of the gods have now come to their fullness: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: mo ṣū ṇo atra juhuranta devā mā pūrve agne pitaraḥ padajñāḥ | purāṇyoḥ sadmanoḥ ketur antar mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Let not the gods deceive us here, O Agni, nor the forefather who know the track; the banner stands between the two ancient dwellings: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: vi me purutrā patayanti kāmāḥ śamy acchā dīdye pūrvyāṇi | samiddhe agnāv ṛtam id vadema mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: My desires fly apart in many directions; toward the fire-staff the ancient things shine forth; at the kindled fire let us speak only truth: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: samāno rājā vibhṛtaḥ purutrā śaye śayāsu prayuto vanānu | anyā vatsam bharati kṣeti mātā mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The one king, spread over many places, lies down in the resting places, sent forth along the forests; one mother carries the calf and dwells apart: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: ākṣit pūrvāsv aparā anūrut sadyo jātāsu taruṇīṣv antaḥ | antarvatīḥ suvate apravītā mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: He has occupied the earlier ones; the later has spread further within the young ones just born; the pregnant ones bring forth without having been approached: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: śayuḥ parastād adha nu dvimātābandha naś carati vatsa ekaḥ | mitrasya tā varuṇasya vratāni mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: There lies a dweller; then the one calf with two mothers wanders unbound; these are the ordinances of Mitra and Varuṇa: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: dvimātā hotā vidatheṣu samrāḻ anv agraṁ carati kṣeti budhnaḥ | pra raṇyāni raṇyavāco bharante mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The priest with two mothers is the sovereign at the assemblies; following the first, he dwells upon the foundation; they carry forth the joys, those whose speech is joyous: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: śūrasyeva yudhyato antamasya pratīcīnaṁ dadṛśe viśvam āyat | antar matiś carati niṣṣidhaṁ gor mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Like that of the most intimate hero in combat, all that approaches is seen face to face; the insight moves within what is settled of the cow: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: ni veveti palito dūta āsv antar mahāmś carati rocanena | vapūṁṣi bibhrad abhi no vi caṣṭe mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The grey-haired one flashes back and forth among them as messenger; the great one moves within them with luminous splendour; bearing forms, he looks out upon us: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: viṣṇur gopāḥ paramam pāti pāthaḥ priyā dhāmāny amṛtā dadhānaḥ | agniṣ ṭā viśvā bhuvanāni veda mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Viṣṇu the protector guards the highest station, bearing the beloved immortal abodes; Agni knows all these beings: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: nānā cakrāte yamyā3 vapūṁṣi tayor anyad rocate kṛṣṇam anyat | śyāvī ca yad aruṣī ca svasārau mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The two siblings, twin-like, have made their forms separate; of the two, one shines dark, the other differently; when the dark one and the ruddy one are sisters: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: mātā ca yatra duhitā ca dhenū sabardughe dhāpayete samīcī | ṛtasya te sadasīḻe antar mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Where mother and daughter, both milch cows, milk together in unison and give suck face to face — I praise them within the seat of holy law: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: anyasyā vatsaṁ rihatī mimāya kayā bhuvā ni dadhe dhenur ūdhaḥ | ṛtasya sā payasāpinvateḻā mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Licking another's calf, she measured out; in what manner does the cow lay down her udder? By the milk of holy law does Iḷā fill it: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: padyā vaste pururūpā vapūṁṣy ūrdhvā tasthaur tryaviṁ rerihāṇā | ṛtasya sadma vi carāmi vidvān mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Clothing herself in footsteps, many-formed in shapes, she has stood erect licking the three-year-old; knowing this, I wander through the seat of holy law: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: pade iva nihite dasme antas tayor anyad guhyam āvir anyat | sadhrīcīnā pathyā3 sā viṣūcī mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: As if laid in a footprint, wondrous, between the two — one hidden, the other manifest; that path going together yet running in different directions: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: ā dhenavo dhunayantām aśiśvīḥ sabardughāḥ śaśayā apradugdhāḥ | navyā-navyā yuvatayo bhavantīr mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Let the cows low, those not suckled, milking together, lying down, not yet fully milked; ever becoming newer and newer as young maidens: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: yad anyāsu vṛṣabho roravīti so anyasmin yūthe ni dadhāti retaḥ | sa hi kṣapāvān sa bhagaḥ sa rājā mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: When the bull bellows among some cows, he deposits seed in another herd; for he is the possessor of night, he is Bhaga, he is the king: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: vīrasya nu svaśvyaṁ janāsaḥ pra nu vocāma vidur asya devāḥ | ṣoḻhā yuktāḥ pañca-pañcā vahanti mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Let us now declare the might of horses of the hero; the gods know of it; thrice six times yoked, they carry five by five: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: devas tvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ pupoṣa prajāḥ purudhā jajāna | imā ca viśvā bhuvanāny asya mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The god Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ, of all forms, has nourished progeny; he has begotten them in manifold ways; and all these beings are his: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: mahī sam airac camvā samīcī ubhe te asya vasunā nyṛṣṭe | śṛṇve vīro vindamāno vasūni mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The great one has brought together two bowls face to face; both have been filled with his treasure; the hero is heard, finding wealth: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: imāṁ ca naḥ pṛthivīṁ viśvadhāyā upa kṣeti hitamitro na rājā | puraḥsadaḥ śarmasado na vīrā mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: Upon this earth of ours, all-sustaining, he dwells as a king who keeps his friends well-disposed; the heroes sit before in safety as if seated in shelter: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: niṣṣidhvarīs ta oṣadhīr utāpo rayiṁ ta indra pṛthivī bibharti | sakhāyas te vāmabhājaḥ syāma mahad devānām asuratvam ekam ||
english: The herbs that restrain, O Indra, the waters and the earth bear wealth for thee; may we be thy friends, partakers of thy bounty: great is the one divine lordship of the gods.

sanskrit: na tā minanti māyino na dhīrā vratā devānām prathamā dhruvāṇi | na rodasī adruhe vedyābhir na parvatā ninamestas thivāṁsaḥ ||
english: Neither the deceitful nor the wise ones transgress the first, firm ordinances of the gods; neither do Heaven and Earth bowing before the altars, nor the mountains that have stood firm.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ bhārām̐ eko acaran bibharty ṛtaṁ varṣiṣṭham upa gāva āguḥ | tisro mahīr aparās tasthu r atyā guhā dve nihite darśy ekā ||
english: The one, moving alone, carries six burdens; the holy law, most abundant, the cows have come up to; three great ones stand above as if on swift horses; two are hidden in secret, one is visible.

sanskrit: tripājasyo vṛṣabho viśvarūpa uta tryudhā purudhā prajāvān | tryanīkaḥ patyate māhināvān sa retodhā vṛṣabhaḥ śaśvatīnām ||
english: The bull of triple gait, of all forms, likewise three-weaponed, prolific in many forms, of three faces, rules as one of greatness; he the seed-depositor, the bull of eternal ones.

sanskrit: abhīka āsām padavīr abodhy ādityānām ahve cāru nāma | āpaś cid asmā aramanta devīḥ pṛthag vrajantīḥ pari ṣīm avṛñjan ||
english: The path of these ones was suddenly awakened; the lovely name of the Ādityas was called out; even the divine waters rested for him; going separately, they encompassed him on every side.

sanskrit: trī ṣadhā sthā sindhava triḥ kavīnām uta trimātā vidatheṣu samrāṭ | ṛtāvarīr yoṣaṇās tisro apyās trir ā divo vidathe patya mānāḥ ||
english: Three stations of the rivers, three of the wise ones, and the sovereign at the assembly has three mothers; the three holy women who keep the law, those sunk in the waters, ruling three times in the assembly from heaven.

sanskrit: trir ā divaḥ savitar vāryāṇi dive-diva ā suva trir no ahnaḥ | tridhātu rāya ā suvā vasūni bhaga trātar dhiṣaṇe sātaye dhāḥ ||
english: Three times from heaven, O Savitṛ, impel the desirable things; day by day drive them thrice for us through the day; drive to us wealth of threefold nature; O Bhaga, O protector, O Dhiṣaṇā, set them for our gaining.

sanskrit: trir ā divaḥ savitā soṣavīti rājānā mitrāvaruṇā supāṇī | āpaś cid asya rodasī cid urvī ratnam bhikṣanta savituḥ savāya ||
english: Savitṛ has driven three times from heaven; the two kings Mitra and Varuṇa, of fair hands; even the waters and the wide Heaven and Earth beg for the gem at the driving-forth of Savitṛ.

sanskrit: trir uttamā dūṇaśā rocanāni trayo rājananty asurasya vīrāḥ | ṛtāvāna iṣirā dūḻabhāsas trir ā divo vidathe santu devāḥ ||
english: Three highest, hard to assail are the luminous realms; three are the heroes of the lord of might who rule; may the gods who keep holy law, the vigorous, hard to reach, be present three times in the assembly from heaven.

sanskrit: pra me vivikv ām̐ avidan manīṣāṁ dhenuṁ carantīm prayutām agopām | sadyaś cid yā duduhe bhūri dhāser indras tad agniḥ panitāro asyāḥ ||
english: The discerning one has found my insight, the cow roaming freely, sent forth, without a herdsman; she who even now has milked abundantly from the overflowing — Indra and Agni are the admirers of her.

sanskrit: indraḥ su pūṣā vṛṣaṇā suhastā divo na prītāḥ śaśayaṁ duduhre | viśve yad asyāṁ raṇayanta devāḥ pra vo 'tra vasavaḥ sumnam aśyām ||
english: Indra and Pūṣan, both bulls, of fair hands, well pleased as from heaven, have milked what lay still; when all the gods shall delight in her, may I here attain the favour of the Vasus.

sanskrit: yā jāmayo vṛṣṇa icchanti śaktiṁ namasyantīr jānate garbham asmin | acchā putraṁ dhenavo vāvaśānā mahaś caranti bibharataṁ vapūṁṣi ||
english: Those who are the kinswomen who desire the power of the bull, reverently honouring them, knowing the embryo within — the cows calling aloud go toward the son, bearing splendid forms.

sanskrit: acchā vivakmi rodasī sumeke grāvṇo yujāno adhvare manīṣā | imā u te manave bhūrivārā ūrdhvā bhavanti darśatā yajat rāḥ ||
english: I speak forth to Heaven and Earth, both fair-thighed, with insight yoked to the pressing stones at the rite; these many-choiced, visible, worthy-of-worship gifts of thine for the sacrificer rise upward, O Manu.

sanskrit: yā te jihvā madhumatī sumedhā agne deveṣūcyata urūcī | tayeha viśvām̐ avase yajat rān ā sādaya pāyayā cā madhūni ||
english: That tongue of thine, honey-sweet, O Agni, wide-reaching, the wise one, called out among the gods — with it seat here all the worthy-of-worship ones for our protection; and cause them to drink the sweet drinks.

sanskrit: yā te agne parvatasyeva dhārāsaścantī pīpayad deva citrā | tām asmabhyam pramatiṁ jātavedo vaso rāsva sumatiṁ viśvajanyām ||
english: That care of thine which shines gloriously, O god, following like a stream from the mountain, which nourishes — grant that care to us, O Jātavedas, O Vasu; grant us the goodwill that belongs to all people.
